questions.question: An MRI shows a midline, slit-like cavity between the two thalami. Which ventricle is being identified?
questions.explanation: The third ventricle is a midline cavity between the thalami and hypothalamic regions.

questions.question: A tumor occupies a ventricular cavity posterior to the pons and upper medulla and anterior to the cerebellum. Which ventricle contains the tumor?
questions.explanation: The fourth ventricle lies between the brainstem anteriorly and cerebellum posteriorly.

questions.question: A lesion lies within the extension of a lateral ventricle into the frontal lobe, anterior to the interventricular foramen. Which part is involved?
questions.explanation: The anterior horn extends into the frontal lobe.

questions.question: Imaging shows a cyst within the temporal lobe extension of the lateral ventricle. Which part contains the cyst?
questions.explanation: The inferior horn extends into the temporal lobe.

questions.question: A ventricular catheter tip is positioned in the occipital lobe extension of the lateral ventricle. Where is the tip located?
questions.explanation: The posterior horn extends into the occipital lobe.

questions.question: During surgery, a thin sheet of white matter stretching between the superior cerebellar peduncles is identified in the upper roof of the fourth ventricle. What is it?
options: Tela choroidea of the third ventricle
questions.explanation: The superior medullary velum forms the upper part of the fourth ventricular roof.

questions.question: A focal lesion affects the facial colliculus in the floor of the fourth ventricle. Which anatomical relationship produces this elevation?
options: Facial nerve fibers looping around the abducens nucleus
Trigeminal nerve fibers looping around the facial nucleus
Hypoglossal fibers looping around the vagal nucleus
Vestibular fibers looping around the cochlear nucleus
questions.explanation: The facial colliculus is formed by the underlying abducens nucleus and looping facial nerve fibers.

questions.question: During inspection of the medullary part of the fourth ventricular floor, a surgeon identifies the hypoglossal trigone. Which nucleus lies beneath it?
options: Dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus
questions.explanation: The hypoglossal trigone overlies the hypoglossal nucleus.

questions.question: A lesion damages the lamina terminalis and anterior commissure. Which wall of the third ventricle is involved?
questions.explanation: The lamina terminalis and anterior commissure contribute to the anterior wall.

questions.question: A mass projects into the third ventricle from the region of the optic chiasm, infundibulum, and mammillary bodies. Which boundary is involved?
questions.explanation: These structures contribute to the floor of the third ventricle.
